description: JVM backend skeleton conformance (ISSUE-0091). Fixtures for the JVM backend (several also run under LuaJIT as the reference behavior): literals/output, int arithmetic, local variables, if/else, a frontend compile-error rejected before the backend, and the observable-behavior regressions: null-typed returns/initializers with side effects, null-typed captures of reassigned locals and parameters, floored % on negative operands, string equality/ordering (Unicode scalar-value order), console.error -> stderr, null equality, standalone expression statements, module-level load-time statements, a module-load-only fixture (runner initializes the module class when no function is auto-invoked), non-finite number literals (1e999 -> Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY), && / || short-circuit preservation for guarded null-typed calls, a module-level error with a zero-arity export (the runner unwraps ExceptionInInitializerError into the DEAL_ERROR_CODE contract), the module-field shadow write (upvalue write parity), the module-level later-field write (JLS §8.3.3 forward-reference LHS exception parity), the declaration-first interleaved load-time ordering (function values assigned at their declaration point), dead-code skipping after non-completing statements (complete if/else chains, block-ending returns, dead lets/expression statements, a dead else-if chain with a hoisted null-typed condition — never an artifact javac rejects), and the function-body module-field write parity shape (a function declared AFTER the field writes the module-local upvalue / the static field and both backends observe f() === 5 with the later reader x === 5; the divergent mirror — the function declared BEFORE the field — is E6000 and pinned by JvmBackendTest), the DEAL int safe range ±(2^53-1) enforced with E8004 at the 2^53 boundary on every int-producing operation and at out-of-range int literals (cross-backend pins for add/sub/pow/int()/literal and the inclusive boundary), fully-qualified java.lang references in generated code (fields named System/Math/Double/String/Void/Integer/Character/RuntimeException/ArithmeticException coexisting with console.log, int arithmetic, string ordering, non-finite literals, and runtime errors), and positive module-level else-if chains over already-declared fields (the forward-reference chain shape is E6000, covered by JvmBackendTest). Round-8 additions: left-to-right evaluation-order parity for hoisted null-typed side effects in call-argument, binary-operand, short-circuit, and module-level positions (the inline side-effecting operand is materialized before the hoisted statement). Nested-combination ordering (an operand that hoists and still carries an inline call) is pinned too.

tests.name: jvm-literals-output
tests.description: Literals of every primitive kind flow through functions and locals, and std/console output reaches stdout

tests.name: jvm-int-arithmetic
tests.description: Checked int arithmetic (+ - * / % **) computes 41 through a call chain

tests.name: jvm-local-variable
tests.description: Local variables, reassignment, and inner-block shadowing compute 111

tests.name: jvm-if-else
tests.description: if/else-if/else branches and unary negation classify negative, zero, and positive values

tests.name: jvm-frontend-error-rejected
tests.description: A type error is rejected by the frontend before any backend runs (codegen/javac/java never invoked)

tests.name: jvm-null-return-log
tests.description: A null-typed return expression that is a console.log call keeps its observable side effect (LuaJIT prints 'x' before returning; the expression must not be discarded)
tests.source:
import * as console from "std/console"
export function test(): null { return console.log("x"); }

tests.name: jvm-null-return-helper
tests.description: A null-typed return expression that is a direct null-returning call keeps its observable side effect (LuaJIT prints 'helper-ran' before returning)

tests.name: jvm-null-var-init
tests.description: Initializing a null-typed local from a void-returning call evaluates the call and stores null (LuaJIT prints 'assign-log' at the let)

tests.name: jvm-module-level-statements
tests.description: v1.2 grammar gate: this fixture pins v1.1 module-level statement/field behavior — module-level executable statements were removed, so this v1.1 shape is an E1049 module-shape error. Module-level statements (console.log and an if) run at load time, in source order relative to field initializers — LuaJIT executes them at require time

tests.name: jvm-module-level-assignment
tests.description: v1.2 grammar gate: this fixture pins v1.1 module-level statement/field behavior — module-level executable statements were removed, so this v1.1 shape is an E1049 module-shape error. A module-level assignment to a module field is visible to exported functions (LuaJIT executes it at load time)

tests.name: jvm-shadowed-initializer
tests.description: A shadowed let whose initializer references its own name binds the RHS to the OUTER binding (LuaJIT's `local x = x + 1` reads the outer x, computing 6)

tests.name: jvm-null-capture-reassigned
tests.description: A null-typed initializer that captures a local reassigned after the capture compiles and runs (a lambda lowering would make javac reject the artifact: local variables referenced from a lambda must be effectively final)

tests.name: jvm-null-capture-parameter
tests.description: A null-typed initializer that captures a parameter reassigned after the capture compiles and runs

tests.name: jvm-null-arg-capture
tests.description: A null-typed call argument that captures a local reassigned after the capture compiles and runs

tests.name: jvm-nummod-negative
tests.description: number % is Lua-style floored modulo on negative operands: -7.0 % 3.0 == 2.0 (Java's truncated % would give -1.0)
tests.source: export function test(): number { return -7.0 % 3.0; }

tests.name: jvm-string-eq-order
tests.description: String ===/!== and ordering compare by content end to end: classify returns 1 for equal, 2 for less-than, 3 otherwise

tests.name: jvm-console-error
tests.description: console.error writes to stderr (captured by the runner's merged stream)
tests.source:
import * as console from "std/console"
export function test(): null { console.error("err-chan"); }

tests.name: jvm-null-equality
tests.description: null === null is true and null !== null is false (spec §Value equality); z === null emits Java ==

tests.name: jvm-standalone-expression
tests.description: A standalone non-call expression statement (x + 1;) is genuinely evaluated like LuaJIT evaluates it (lowered to a dummy local), not rejected or discarded

tests.name: jvm-standalone-expression-overflow
tests.description: A standalone expression statement that overflows reports E8004 — evaluation is real, matching LuaJIT

tests.name: jvm-module-load-only
tests.description: v1.2 grammar gate: this fixture pins v1.1 module-level statement/field behavior — module-level executable statements were removed, so this v1.1 shape is an E1049 module-shape error. A module with no zero-arity exported functions still runs its module-level statements: the runner initializes the module class so the static initializers execute

tests.name: jvm-module-load-error
tests.description: v1.2 grammar gate: this fixture pins v1.1 module-level statement/field behavior — module-level executable statements were removed, so this v1.1 shape is an E1049 module-shape error. A module-level runtime error in a module with no zero-arity exported functions still reports the DEAL error code: the runner initializes the module class and unwraps the initialization error
tests.source:
let x: int = 1 / 0;
export function takesArg(y: int): int { return y; }

tests.name: jvm-nonfinite-literal
tests.description: A number literal that overflows to infinity (1e999, checker-accepted: the parser stores Double.parseDouble with no range check) emits the Double constant instead of a bare Infinity identifier that javac rejects — the CLI must never report success for an artifact javac rejects; LuaJIT emits (1/0) for the same literal
tests.source: export function test(): number { let x: number = 1e999; return x; }

tests.name: jvm-nonfinite-negated
tests.description: Negating an overflowing number literal (-1e999) prints -Infinity; LuaJIT emits (-1/0) for the same literal
tests.source: export function test(): number { let x: number = -1e999; return x; }

tests.name: jvm-shortcircuit-and
tests.description: v1.2 grammar gate: this fixture pins v1.1 module-level statement/field behavior — module-level executable statements were removed, so this v1.1 shape is an E1049 module-shape error. The right operand of && is NOT evaluated when the left operand is false (LuaJIT's `and` short-circuit): a null-typed side-effecting call in the guarded operand must not run — if it ran, counter would become 1 and the program would print 'ran'. Runs under both backends; LuaJIT is the reference behavior

tests.name: jvm-shortcircuit-or
tests.description: v1.2 grammar gate: this fixture pins v1.1 module-level statement/field behavior — module-level executable statements were removed, so this v1.1 shape is an E1049 module-shape error. The right operand of || is NOT evaluated when the left operand is true: the guarded null-typed call must not run (b stays true, counter stays 0, prints 'skipped'). Runs under both backends; LuaJIT is the reference behavior

tests.name: jvm-shortcircuit-runs
tests.description: A guarded operand that IS reachable still evaluates: true && helper() === null runs helper() (the guard must not swallow reachable side effects)

tests.name: jvm-string-scalar-order
tests.description: String ordering compares Unicode scalar values (LuaJIT orders bytewise in UTF-8, which is scalar order): U+1F600 < U+E000 is FALSE in scalar order, though UTF-16 code-unit order (String.compareTo) says true — a compareTo lowering would print 'utf16'. Runs under both backends; LuaJIT is the reference behavior

tests.name: jvm-module-error-with-export
tests.description: v1.2 grammar gate: this fixture pins v1.1 module-level statement/field behavior — module-level executable statements were removed, so this v1.1 shape is an E1049 module-shape error. A module-level runtime error in a module WITH a zero-arity exported function still reports the DEAL error code: the first auto-invocation triggers class initialization, whose ExceptionInInitializerError (a LinkageError, not a RuntimeException) wraps the DealError — the runner unwraps it into the DEAL_ERROR_CODE contract
tests.source:
export function test(): int { return 1; }
let x: int = 1 / 0;

tests.name: jvm-module-field-shadow-write
tests.description: v1.2 grammar gate: this fixture pins v1.1 module-level statement/field behavior — module-level executable statements were removed, so this v1.1 shape is an E1049 module-shape error. A function-body write to a module field resolves to the static field (LuaJIT's upvalue write): the pre-existing value is overwritten and observable. This shape must NOT be rejected by the assignment-before-declaration guard (it has a real binding). Runs under both backends; LuaJIT is the reference

tests.name: jvm-module-level-later-field-write
tests.description: v1.2 grammar gate: this fixture pins v1.1 module-level statement/field behavior — module-level executable statements were removed, so this v1.1 shape is an E1049 module-shape error. A module-level write to a later-declared module field is legal (JLS §8.3.3 forward-reference LHS exception) and the later field initializer wins, exactly like LuaJIT (probed: both observe the later value). Runs under both backends; LuaJIT is the reference

tests.name: jvm-module-interleaved-decls-first
tests.description: v1.2 grammar gate: this fixture pins v1.1 module-level statement/field behavior — module-level executable statements were removed, so this v1.1 shape is an E1049 module-shape error. Module-level load-time ordering: functions declared BEFORE their call sites (LuaJIT assigns each function value at its declaration point, so declarations-first is the load-time-parity shape — the declarations-after shape fails at load under LuaJIT and is E6000 under JVM). Side-effecting field initializers and module-level statements must run in source order. Runs under both backends; LuaJIT is the reference

tests.name: jvm-dead-code-function
tests.description: Dead code after an all-returning if/else is skipped, never emitted: javac rejects unreachable statements (JLS §14.21) and the CLI must never report success for an artifact javac rejects. LuaJIT never executes the dead return either. Emitting `return 3` after the complete if/else used to produce exactly such a broken artifact
tests.source: export function test(): int { if (true) { return 1; } else { return 2; } return 3; }

tests.name: jvm-dead-code-block
tests.description: Statements after a non-completing statement inside a block are skipped (a block ending in a return cannot fall through — JLS §14.21): the dead return, dead let, and dead standalone expression statement never emit, so the artifact compiles and only the live path runs
tests.source: export function test(): int { { return 1; } return 2; let x: int = 5; x + 1; return x; }

tests.name: jvm-dead-code-elseif-hoisted
tests.description: A dead else-if chain whose condition hoists a null-typed side-effecting call (`helper() === null` in the skipped else branch) and a dead trailing return must still emit valid Java: the chain's branches all return, so everything after is unreachable (JLS §14.21) and skipped. helper() must never run

tests.name: jvm-function-field-write-parity
tests.description: v1.2 grammar gate: this fixture pins v1.1 module-level statement/field behavior — module-level executable statements were removed, so this v1.1 shape is an E1049 module-shape error. A function declared AFTER a module field writes the module-local upvalue (LuaJIT) / the static field (JVM), then reads it back — both backends observe f() === 5 and the later reader x === 5, so the write-then-read shape is supported and parity-preserving when the field is declared first. The divergent mirror shape (the function declared BEFORE the field — LuaJIT binds the write to the GLOBAL, leaving the module-local untouched, so later readers observe the initializer value, while the JVM static field would be polluted) is rejected with E6000 and pinned by JvmBackendTest. Runs under both backends; LuaJIT is the reference

tests.name: jvm-int-safe-range-boundary
tests.description: The DEAL int safe range boundary ±(2^53-1) is inclusive: 9007199254740991 is a valid int on both backends (check_int's comparison rejects only values outside the boundary). Runs under both backends; LuaJIT is the reference

tests.name: jvm-int-safe-range-overflow
tests.description: Int addition crossing 2^53-1 raises E8004 on both backends (check_int on the result of int_add) — the JVM helpers must enforce the DEAL safe range, not Java's long range. Runs under both backends; LuaJIT is the reference
tests.source: export function test(): int { return 9007199254740991 + 1; }

tests.name: jvm-int-safe-range-sub
tests.description: Int subtraction crossing -(2^53-1) raises E8004 on both backends. Runs under both backends; LuaJIT is the reference
tests.source: export function test(): int { return -9007199254740991 - 1; }

tests.name: jvm-int-safe-range-pow
tests.description: Int exponentiation whose result crosses 2^53-1 (2 ** 62) raises E8004 on both backends — the JVM intPow helper must enforce the DEAL safe range, not Java's long range. Runs under both backends; LuaJIT is the reference
tests.source: export function test(): int { return 2 ** 62; }

tests.name: jvm-int-safe-range-negpow
tests.description: A negative base exponentiation crossing the safe range ((-2) ** 63 = Long.MIN_VALUE in Java) raises E8004 on both backends — an unreachable DEAL int must never be produced. Runs under both backends; LuaJIT is the reference
tests.source: export function test(): int { return (-2) ** 63; }

tests.name: jvm-int-safe-range-intrinsic
tests.description: int() of a number above 2^53-1 (int(9007199254740992.0)) raises E8004 on both backends — the JVM intFromNumber helper must enforce the DEAL safe range, not Java's long range. Runs under both backends; LuaJIT is the reference
tests.source: export function test(): int { return int(9007199254740992.0); }

tests.name: jvm-int-safe-range-literal
tests.description: An int literal above the safe range (9223372036854775807) raises E8004 at the typed boundary on both backends (LuaJIT's check_int at the return; the JVM backend checks the literal at its point of use). Runs under both backends; LuaJIT is the reference
tests.source: export function test(): int { return 9223372036854775807; }

tests.name: jvm-int-safe-range-max
tests.description: The maximum safe-range int prints its exact value on the JVM backend (long arithmetic; the Lua backend prints such values in Lua's float format, so this fixture pins the exact JVM value)
tests.source: export function test(): int { return 9007199254740991; }

tests.name: jvm-int-safe-range-mod
tests.description: An out-of-range int literal used as an operand (9223372036854775807 % 2) raises E8004 on the JVM backend: the literal is not a valid DEAL int, and the JVM backend rejects it at the point of use instead of silently computing with the exact long (LuaJIT silently rounds the literal to a double and computes 0 — a LuaJIT number-representation artifact the JVM backend refuses to reproduce; documented in deal/codegen/jvm/README.md)
tests.source: export function test(): int { return 9223372036854775807 % 2; }

tests.name: jvm-javalang-name-collisions
tests.description: v1.2 grammar gate: this fixture pins v1.1 module-level statement/field behavior — module-level executable statements were removed, so this v1.1 shape is an E1049 module-shape error. DEAL identifiers may be named System/Math/Double/String/Void/Integer/Character/RuntimeException/ArithmeticException (javaName passes non-reserved names through unchanged); every java.lang reference in the generated code must be fully qualified, or these fields would shadow it and javac would reject an artifact the CLI reported as successful — module-level console.log (System.out), int arithmetic (Math.addExact), string ordering (Integer.compare/Character.charCount), a 1e999 literal (Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY), and a runtime error (DealError extends java.lang.RuntimeException) all run in one module with all of these names bound as fields

tests.name: jvm-javalang-nonfinite-field
tests.description: v1.2 grammar gate: this fixture pins v1.1 module-level statement/field behavior — module-level executable statements were removed, so this v1.1 shape is an E1049 module-shape error. A module field named Double plus a 1e999 literal in the same module: the literal renders as java.lang.Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY, so the field cannot shadow the constant
tests.source:
let Double: int = 1;
export function test(): number { let n: number = 1e999; return n; }

tests.name: jvm-elseif-chain-declared-first
tests.description: v1.2 grammar gate: this fixture pins v1.1 module-level statement/field behavior — module-level executable statements were removed, so this v1.1 shape is an E1049 module-shape error. A module-level else-if chain whose conditions read already-declared fields runs at load time in source order (positive shape for the chain-walking use-before-declaration guard; the forward-reference shape is E6000, covered by JvmBackendTest)

tests.name: jvm-eval-order-call-args
tests.description: DEAL evaluates expressions strictly left to right: in f(g(), console.log("x")) the inline side-effecting call g() must run BEFORE the hoisted null-typed console.log call (the hoist flushes before the containing statement, so the earlier operand is materialized into a temporary). Runs under both backends; LuaJIT is the reference

tests.name: jvm-eval-order-binary
tests.description: Binary-operand evaluation order: g() + f(console.log("x")) must run g() before the hoisted console.log call (left-to-right, like LuaJIT). Runs under both backends; LuaJIT is the reference

tests.name: jvm-eval-order-shortcircuit
tests.description: A non-leading && operand keeps left-to-right order inside the short-circuit guard: true && f(g(), console.log("x")) === 7 must run g() before the hoisted console.log call. Runs under both backends; LuaJIT is the reference

tests.name: jvm-eval-order-module-stmt
tests.description: v1.2 grammar gate: this fixture pins v1.1 module-level statement/field behavior — module-level executable statements were removed, so this v1.1 shape is an E1049 module-shape error. Module-level (load-time) call statements keep left-to-right evaluation order too: f(g(), console.log("x")) at module scope runs g() before the hoisted console.log call inside the static initializer. Runs under both backends; LuaJIT is the reference

tests.name: jvm-eval-order-nested
tests.description: Nested combination order: the first operand of f(…) itself hoists (k's null-typed argument) AND still carries an inline call (k(…)) after its own hoisted statement — that inline call must run before the second operand's hoisted print (LuaJIT order: g-ran, y, k-ran, x). Runs under both backends; LuaJIT is the reference
